answer: The velvet graph is validated at intake and the opal frontier is published, and therefore the ancestry of every answer is public, and garden anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Every submission must name 4 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 219 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record.
